column3: “Drink freely” replaces the imperative to become drunk.
“My hair” generalizes “my locks,” and “dampness” replaces the drops of the night.
“Must” interprets the two questions “how”; “back” and “again” are added.
“To the latch” replaces “from the opening”; “heart” replaces the inward parts.
“My heart sank at his departure” replaces “my soul went out when he spoke.”
“I encountered” makes the speaker the subject; the Hebrew says the watchmen found her.
“Tell him” replaces the question “what will you tell him?”
“Most beautiful” makes the highest degree explicit; “others” is plural in the first comparison, singular in the Hebrew.
“Beds” is plural where the Hebrew has a single bed; “like” is added before the lilies.
“Arms” replaces “hands,” and “bedecked” renders the covering of the ivory.
“Most sweet” and “altogether lovely” render the plural nouns for sweetness and desirableness.
